title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
claim: Small oxoanion templates are essential for high-nuclearity lanthanide-containing clusters, but their concentration must stay low; slow release by in situ ligand decomposition or uptake of atmospheric CO2 avoids precipitating lanthanide salts and allows modular growth.
explanation: Direct addition of oxoanions tends to precipitate insoluble lanthanide salts. Carbonate from IDA decomposition, DMF decomposition, or atmospheric CO2, and oxalate/glycolate from IDA, occupy faces or coordination sites and support double-shell or four-shell frameworks. Multiple anions can each template a fragment that later joins into a larger cage with internal voids.
scope: Giant lanthanide and 3d–4f hydroxide clusters templated by nitrate, carbonate, and related small anions.
conditions: Low template concentration; hydro/solvothermal in situ anion generation or atmospheric CO2 absorption rather than stoichiometric addition of the anion salt.
caveats: The same ligand system is highly condition-sensitive: La versus smaller Pr, or a higher pH, switches among La20Ni30, Pr20Ni21, and Gd54Ni54. Template origin is often inferred, not always independently quantified.
